blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415). The r418-r421 shutdown hang (an unconditional, timeout-less thread.join() blocking forever on a worker thread stuck acquiring the global g_dpc_level_mutex inside KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel, orphaned when GuestThreadTerminated unwinds a thread between its Raise and matching Lower) is FIXED and LIVE-VERIFIED (r422): raise_dpc_level()/lower_dpc_level()/release_residual_dpc_level() (native/include/ac6/native_guest_threads.h, native/src/native_guest_threads.cpp) with a thread_local depth counter let every GuestThreadTerminated catch site release whatever IRQL depth that thread still holds instead of orphaning the mutex; 4 independent standalone launches (incl. one with AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE=1, the original r418 trigger) all exit cleanly; native ctest 10/10, full product pytest 222/1-skip, repo gates and root ctest green. No known blocker remains anywhere in the r399-r422 chain. r423 is a traceability correction, not a technical finding: r422's commit (2c07b1ec) swept in a backlog of nine prior uncommitted cycles (r239, r240, r255, r276, r278, r280, r281, r282, r285, r286) on three files alongside its own IRQL fix, undisclosed in that commit's message -- content is sound (already covered by r422's own passing test runs, and there's direct precedent for backlog catch-up commits, e0afccdd), so no revert/amend was done, just documentation naming what was actually included. Named for r424 (lowest-cost open thread, not a blocker): add a targeted unit/integration test that directly simulates 'raised IRQL then GuestThreadTerminated' to cover the r421/r422 regression class going forward. Separately, r418's presented_frames=0/present=0 question (the per-frame loop runs but the guest never emits a Present packet in the observed window) remains open as the next PRODUCT question, now uncomplicated by any shutdown hang. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched beyond what r422 already swept in -- reports and named tool/source changes for r413-r423 were committed individually.
